background: Nationwide Building Society is the largest building society in the world and the UK's second-largest mortgage lender, a mutual funded by retail savings and current accounts and lending mainly on residential mortgages, now also the owner of Virgin Money.
synthesis: Ratings are AA- from Fitch after the upgrade on 12 May 2026, A+ from S&P and A1 from Moody's, all stable, the highest of any UK building society. Capital is mixed against UK building societies: CET1 of 18.6% is above the 17.8% median, but leverage of 5.2% is in the bottom quarter against 6.1%. Liquidity is also mixed, with LCR of 174% below the 214% median and NSFR of 145% at the median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods. The flagged news on 29 Jun 2026 and 2 Jul 2026 is job cuts following the Virgin Money takeover, a cost measure rather than a credit event.
